$schema-note: The committed per-file test-only exclusion list for the third-party coverage study (issue #676): language -> pin -> sorted relative paths. Read and diffed by tools/coverage-study/coverage_table.py, which .github/workflows/coverage-study.yml runs after the measuring jobs. GENERATED — regenerate it with `coverage_table.py --write` rather than editing it by hand; the renderer rejects an unsorted or duplicated list.
$why-note: baseline.json records HOW MANY files each Tier A harness took out of the denominator; this file records WHICH. A count alone cannot state the property that matters: a PARTIAL readmission (34 -> 31, three files back in the denominator) is arithmetically identical to "the pin's test suite shrank by 3 while its library grew by 3", so `scored`, `clean`, the stage-1 funnel and the #648 total-collapse check are all satisfied by it, and the run reads as an ordinary raise onto a population nobody chose. Diffing the paths needs no such inference: a path recorded here that a run SCORED was readmitted, and the breach names the file. A path that is merely GONE is not a breach — the pin may have deleted it — so only positive evidence fires, the same rule the count-based check follows.
$workflow-note: WHEN A PIN'S TEST POPULATION LEGITIMATELY CHANGES: update this file in the SAME reviewed PR that moves the pin, by running the study and committing the regenerated list. That is the whole point of committing it — the change stops being an invisible arithmetic wobble and becomes a diff a reviewer reads. On main the publish job regenerates and commits it exactly the way it raises baseline.json. A row that excludes nothing is declared as an empty object; an ABSENT language key is a hard failure, because it would leave that row's exclusions diffed against nothing.
